findings.situation: A filer deducted royalty losses in full on earlier returns without filing Form 6198, because their whole investment was at risk, and their amount at risk has now fallen below zero; they truthfully answer No.
findings.source_text: p925 p. 19, At-Risk Limits: "If your losses from an at-risk activity are allowed, they're subject to recapture in later years if your amount at risk is reduced below zero." and "File Form 6198 with your tax return if: a. You have a loss ... and b. You aren't at risk for some of your investment in the activity."
findings.why: The question only asks whether Form 6198 was filed or a loss was held back. Allowed prior losses with no Form 6198 filed can still be recaptured, and the refusal is meant to cover recapture of losses allowed before. Without a question about prior losses deducted from the royalty, that case passes the gate.

locators: p. 19, At-Risk Limits, "You treat any loss that is disallowed because of the at-risk limits as a deduction from the same activity in the next tax year"

p. 19, At-Risk Limits, "You treat any loss that is disallowed because of the at-risk limits as a deduction from the same activity in the next tax year. If your losses from an at-risk activity are allowed, they’re subject to recapture in later years if your amount at risk is reduced below zero."
